key_takeaways: Two Australians with no German address can register to marry in Germany: under § 12 of the Civil Status Act, the Standesamt before which the marriage is to take place receives the registration.

German civil law expects a certificate of capacity to marry from your home country, but from 1 December 2021 the Australian Embassy Berlin and Consulate-General Frankfurt stopped issuing CNIs, and German authorities have been advised you should not be required to provide one.

The Embassy's guideline lists a birth certificate no older than six months with a certified German translation and a single status declaration from your state or territory registry of births, deaths and marriages; the Standesamt sets the final list.

Timing runs on six-month windows: Berlin accepts registration no earlier than six months ahead, the Standesamt's confirmation lapses after six months, and Berlin's exemption takes at least three weeks.
Marrying legally in Australia first (NOIM at least one month ahead) takes every German legal step out of your wedding week.

faq.q: How much does it cost to get married in Germany?
faq.a: Fees vary by place. Berlin's 2026 fees include EUR 45 to register, plus EUR 45 for each partner whose foreign law must be considered, EUR 40 to marry at another Standesamt and EUR 12 for a certificate. Berlin's Kammergericht charges EUR 15 to 305 (2026) for an exemption, by income and effort.

faq.q: Do you have to speak German to get married in Germany?
faq.a: No, but you need help if you do not. Under § 1312 of the Civil Code, the registrar asks each of you individually whether you wish to marry. Munich asks couples who do not speak German well to bring a publicly appointed, sworn translator to the registration appointment, so plan for language support at both stages.

faq.q: Can you get married in a German castle?
faq.a: Only if your Standesamt can marry you there. Berlin charges EUR 75 to 150 (2026) for a marriage outside its official premises and notes that special wedding locations can add further costs. Otherwise, marry at the Standesamt and celebrate at the castle.

faq.q: Is a marriage in Germany legally recognised in Australia?
faq.a: Generally yes. Smartraveller lists the exceptions: a marriage is not recognised where either person was already married, not old enough, too closely related or forced to marry. It also suggests talking to a lawyer to confirm an overseas certificate is valid in Australia.

faq.q: How long does it take to get married in Germany as a foreigner?
faq.a: Plan backwards from your date. Under § 1309 of the Civil Code, an exemption from the President of the Higher Regional Court is valid for six months only, and a home-country certificate of capacity loses force if you do not marry within six months of issue, or less if stated on it. Your documents, registration and any exemption all have to fall inside that window.
